best_for: Developers on Windows or Mac who need to build and run Linux containers locally, at home or at a company small enough for the free terms.

points.title: Free only below a size line
points.text: The Personal plan is free, and so is use for non-commercial open source. Commercial use is free only at companies with fewer than 250 employees and under USD 10 million in yearly revenue. Larger companies, and all government bodies, need a paid plan.

points.title: Paid plans per user
points.text: Pro is USD 9 a month billed yearly (USD 11 monthly), Team USD 15 billed yearly (USD 16 monthly) for up to 100 users, and Business USD 24 a month billed yearly. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Windows needs the right edition
points.text: It needs Windows 10 22H2 or Windows 11 23H2 or later, 8 GB of RAM and virtualization turned on in the firmware. Windows Server is not supported. Home and Education editions run Linux containers only; Windows containers need Pro or Enterprise.

points.title: Per-user or all-users on Windows
points.text: A per-user install with the WSL 2 backend needs no admin rights after WSL is first enabled. Hyper-V and Windows containers need the all-users install, which is what the installers listed here do. Switching modes means reinstalling.

points.title: Arm64 Windows is early
points.text: The Arm64 Windows build is Early Access: WSL 2 backend only, and no Windows containers.

points.title: Macs: only recent macOS
points.text: Docker supports the current macOS and the two before it, so older Macs drop off each year; the builds listed here need macOS 14 or later. Apple silicon and Intel both have builds, with 4 GB of RAM as the floor.

points.title: Older versions
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 153 versions; macOS lists only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
